Prevention: Provide adequate air circulation by planting at the recommended spacing of 60x90cm.
Avoid planting the crop under shade.
Selectively prune overcrowded plant material to help increase air circulation.
This helps reduce relative humidity and infection.
Avoid overhead irrigation to minimise spread of the fungus.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: beans, carrots, eggplant, pumpkin, melons, tomatoes, snow peas, pepper.
White powdery spots on both sides of the leaf, petiole and stems daily.
Heavily infested leaves which may turn yellow and gradually die.
Take action when one plant is affected.
Direct Control: Mix 1 tablespoon of baking soda with a teaspoon of dormant oil (vegetable or neem oil) and 1 teaspoon of liquid soap in 5 litres of water and spray weekly.
Ensure the crop is completely covered.
Mix one part alcohol based mouthwash and three parts of water and spray the crop weekly.
Spray weekly with a mixture of one part milk to two parts water .
Ensure all the plant is covered completely for proper control.
Remove and burn infected plant parts.
All the above biopesticides should be sprayed at the on-set of the disease.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide always wear protective equipment
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
